task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Can the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile be identified as the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types?
How many absence spells are needed to rank teammates by gain with useful power?
How should profile closeness be defined and validated before testing?
How are regression-to-the-mean and selection effects handled when absences are chosen by injury or rest?
Are play-type initiation labels derived from the same play-by-play used for outcomes, and does that create leakage?

historical_evidence.finding: On/off identity displacement study: 908 player-seasons with at least 400 possessions on and off, 96 usage-matched pairs (caliper 0.03). Shapers showed larger displacement than usage-matched non-shapers (Delta D_A=+0.115, t=6.35, p~7e-9). Correlation of L with D_A was +0.60. Validation status recorded as NOT_RECORDED. This is related to absence-based comparison, but it does not test the teammate-gain ranking question.

Portability feasibility gate: the preregistered gate required at least 25 movers, at least 80% with at least 3 decoys, and |rho|<0.90. The preregistered record had 296 movers with rho=0.048; the final output had 294 movers with rho=0.007. [prior work] notes that mover count and vacuity rho changed between the preregistration record and final output. Gate passed.

Portability confirmatory test: a mover's displacement signature was more similar across franchises than profile-matched destination decoys' signatures (median Delta=+0.0557, permutation p=0.0050, 173/294 positive, sign-test p=2.87e-3, destination-franchise CI [+0.0192,+0.0859]). Its risk is listed as PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE. The preregistered record had Delta=+0.0819 with 296 movers.

Within-game adaptation toward counter play types was associated with higher later PPP (adapter advantage about +0.058 PPP across 531 to 586 rows). Subgroup results were inconsistent (SWITCH reversed), and [prior work] is limited by selection or regression to the mean. Recorded as artifact.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Associating within-game adaptation to counter play types with later scoring gains, using observational adapter versus non-adapter comparisons.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact and limited by selection or regression to the mean. The effect was not stable across subgroups (SWITCH reversed), so the lift is not attributable to adaptation.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project work in this area used usage-matched or profile-matched comparisons with a preregistered gate and decoys, and at least one such design (SF-[prior work]) returned a supported result on a player-absence dataset.
Absence-based and portability designs in this project had to handle sample-size gating and decoy construction, and a feasibility gate was used before confirmatory testing.
Observational comparisons of adapting versus non-adapting groups were flagged as artifacts when selection or regression to the mean was not controlled ([prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: None of the retrieved records tests whether the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types.
No retrieved record reports a ranking test of teammates by profile closeness, minutes, initiations, or same-position minutes.
No record reports a result from the 2022-23 to 2025-26 play-type possession data with 11 absence cases.
The retrieved records do not show that closeness measures for initiation profiles were validated.
own_inferences: With 11 cases, a test that ranks teammates by gain across absences has very little power; a single absence contributes one ranking, so the result would be dominated by a few cases.
The retrieved records use usage-matched or decoy comparisons, which suggests a comparable control would be needed here, but 11 cases may not support decoy-based inference.
The n=148 spells figure is not reconciled with 11 cases; if spells are nested within cases, the effective sample is closer to 11.
The predicted outcome is mostly uncertain or untestable because the design cannot support a stable ranking test at this sample size.
uncertainties: The exact definition of 'closest initiation profile' and the distance metric are not specified.
Whether the 11 cases are players or absence events is unclear, and how the 148 spells map onto them.
The derived play-type labels come from play-by-play and may be affected by how initiations are assigned.
Retrieval returned no record that directly addresses absence-based play-type redistribution, so no prior answer to this specific question is known.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records were used to set the design and the risk list: they supported a usage-matched comparison with a preregistered feasibility gate (SF-[prior work], SF-[prior work]), flagged placebo dependence ([prior work]), and flagged selection and regression to the mean as a limitation ([prior work]). They did not supply evidence that the question is answerable, so the decision was made on the 11-case constraint and the lack of a direct prior test.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 11 cases are available. A ranking test of which teammate gains most will have very low power, and the confirmatory test cannot reach useful power with this data.
Absences are not randomly assigned. Injury or rest choices, and the use of selected 'closest' teammates, can produce apparent gains through regression to the mean, as in [prior work].
Primary play types for a given absent player and their teammates may have very few initiations in the post-absence window, making gain estimates unstable.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record answers the question as posed. SF-[prior work] and [prior work] used usage-matched and decoy-based comparisons with supported results, but on different outcomes (identity displacement and franchise portability). [prior work] was an artifact of selection or regression to the mean. None tests the teammate-gain ranking for absent players' primary play types.

risks.text: Eleven cases cannot support a ranking test of teammate gains with useful power; a single outlier absence can determine the result.
Teammates chosen for being similar or high-usage may show gains due to regression to the mean or selection into the absence window, as recorded for [prior work].
Initiation counts per play type are small, so gain estimates per teammate are noisy.
Initiator and play-type labels are derived from the same play-by-play used for the outcome, so labeling errors or outcome-dependent definitions can create spurious gains.
The profile-closeness measure is not validated; different distance definitions can change which teammate is 'closest'.
Comparing many teammates across several play types and several closeness definitions inflates false positives.
Without decoy or placebo teammates, a gain for the closest teammate cannot be separated from a general increase in usage for high-minute players, as flagged for [prior work].
Minutes, same-position status, and role changes are correlated with both profile closeness and post-absence gains.
[prior work] reports changed mover counts and rho values between the preregistration record and final output (SF-[prior work]), so pipeline versioning must be locked before analysis.

design.estimand: Not applicable as a confirmatory test. Minimum viable test: the difference in mean play-type gain between the closest-profile teammate and the next-closest teammate, averaged across absence cases, with a usage-matched placebo teammate.
design.unit: Absence case (one absent player and one absence window), with teammates nested within cases.
design.sample: 11 absence cases; spells (148) are nested within cases and are not independent. The exact mapping of spells to cases must be confirmed before analysis.
design.power: Not achievable at useful power with 11 cases. Report confidence intervals and do not claim a confirmatory result.
design.controls: Usage-matched placebo teammates, minutes, same-position status, pre-absence play-type shares, and an explicit regression-to-the-mean adjustment using pre-absence rate.
design.falsification: The hypothesis is falsified if the closest-profile teammate's gain does not exceed that of usage-matched placebo teammates in a pre-specified majority of cases.
design.multiplicity: One primary ranking metric pre-specified; secondary play types and closeness definitions reported as exploratory with correction.
design.decision_rule: Confirm only if the closest-profile gain exceeds usage-matched placebo gains with a pre-specified interval excluding zero across cases. Otherwise report as inconclusive; with 11 cases a null result is not an adequately powered rejection.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 play-by-play, with 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13 and 2025-26 playoffs complete from 2026-06-21. Use only data complete as of 2026-11-01 and lock the pipeline before analysis.
